context_title: Your task is to take the provided technical description and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full application with all files, in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code.

entries.answer:
Create a single production-ready HTML application that implements a complete website-building system from scratch, using one descriptive lowercase-hyphenated `.html` file as the entry point and a relative `assets/` directory for generated media, with no server-side code, no storage APIs, no placeholder content, and no separate secret pages. Begin by determining the site type and purpose, then derive the tone from the concept, and use that tone to choose typography, palette, spacing density, layout rhythm, motion intensity, and image style; if no direction is provided, default to a clean Swiss-inspired system with neutral warm surfaces, one restrained teal accent, and minimal functional motion. Build the entire visual system before any page content by defining a full token set in CSS: a fluid `clamp()`-based type scale with a 12px minimum floor, a 4px spacing scale, light and dark theme variables, semantic color roles in OKLCH-oriented layering, radius tokens, motion tokens, shadows, content-width tokens, and font variables `--font-display` and `--font-body` that always use loaded web fonts with system fallbacks only. Include both system-driven dark mode and a manual theme toggle that sets `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on ``, with the initial mode based on `prefers-color-scheme`, no localStorage, and a visible header control for switching themes. Construct a design system proof page first, not the final site, and use it to validate the whole token system visually before proceeding. Create a dedicated `design-test.html` that renders nested surface layers, a type specimen showing display vs. body font boundaries, text on every surface variant for contrast checks, and a small sampler of core UI elements such as primary, secondary, and ghost buttons, a card, an input with label and focus ring, a badge, and a divider; include both light and dark mode in this proof, and do not continue until every surface level is visibly distinct, every text-on-surface combination is readable, and the display font is used only at 24px and above. Use the proof page to confirm that the design remains restrained, that no more than two non-neutral hues appear in a single viewport unless explicitly required, and that the final chosen palette works in both themes with WCAG AA contrast for body text and large text. After validation, remove the proof page from the final deliverable and carry the verified tokens and styles into the real application. Build the final application directly in production code, using semantic HTML structure with exactly one `

` and a proper heading hierarchy, skip link, accessible landmarks, keyboard support, visible focus states, appropriate alt text, and touch targets of at least 44x44px. Use a single scrollable layout with a clear content hierarchy, responsive mobile-first behavior starting at 375px, and fluid expansion up to desktop widths, with content constrained by the appropriate max-width ladder for prose, cards, or full-bleed sections. Use CSS Grid, subgrid where useful, container queries where appropriate, and nested CSS where supported, but keep the composition disciplined: most sections should align to the grid, only one or two moments should break it, and every structural choice should serve readability rather than decoration. Treat forms, cards, navigation, hero areas, and overlays as designed states, not generic containers; every overlay must include a title and a dismiss action, every loading view must have a skeleton matching the real layout, every empty state must explain what belongs there and include an action, every error state must be contextual and specific, and every image failure must have an intentional fallback. Use a restrained, high-quality visual system with intentional typography and color. Load distinctive fonts from Fontshare first, or Google Fonts only if needed, and never rely on system fonts as the primary face; define exactly which font is the display face and which is the body face, and keep the total number of font families to two or three maximum. Keep body copy at 16px by default, use 14px for buttons and navigation, 12px only for tiny labels, and reserve the largest display scale for informational or landing-style hero moments only; for web apps, cap page titles at the equivalent of `--text-xl` and never use hero-scale display typography. Use the neutral surface hierarchy to create depth, tone-match shadows to the palette, use alpha-blended borders instead of solid gray lines, and avoid visual clichés such as gradient buttons, glowing blobs, colored side borders on cards, icon circles, symmetrical three-feature grids, or generic AI-style marketing sections. Keep accent color usage sparse and purposeful, with one primary action per view, and make the layout feel designed through spacing, alignment, and hierarchy rather than decoration. Implement the site with production-grade assets and verified external resources only. Generate real images when the design needs them, place them intentionally in the layout with proper dimensions and lazy loading, and never invent image URLs; all `` elements must use approved sources or generated assets and include `alt`, `width`, `height`, and `loading="lazy"`. Create a custom inline SVG logo for the project, with a simplified favicon variant if needed, and make it geometrically minimal, monochrome-first, and readable at small sizes. Use CDN-hosted libraries only when necessary, defer or module-load JavaScript, avoid heavy dependencies unless justified, and ensure the final page remains performant with lazy loading, `content-visibility` for off-screen content, and a total initial weight appropriate for a high-quality static site. Verify the page at both mobile and desktop widths, adjust the design until the system feels coherent in both light and dark mode, and ensure the final result is a complete, unabridged, production-ready application with all required files and no placeholders, mocks, dummies, or simulated content.
